name: VLSI-CAD
intro: Our Design Automation work spans three areas. For standard CMOS, we develop CAD algorithms, methodologies and prototype tools for low-power, variation-tolerant ICs, focusing on logic and physical synthesis. In Beyond-CMOS, we model Graphene P-N junctions and transistors, and study integration strategies for flexible, ultra-low-power circuits. For Electrical Energy Systems with hybrid sources such as batteries and solar cells, we build system-level simulation frameworks and run-time charge and thermal management.
funded_blurb: Ongoing projects include R2POWER300 and R3POWERUP, which work on 300mm technology for smart power and power discretes, and Lab4MEMS II, on micro-optical MEMS, micro-mirrors and pico-projectors.

paper.title: Design Techniques and Architectures for Low-Leakage SRAMs
paper.authors_full: Andrea Calimera, Alberto Macii, Enrico Macii, Massimo Poncino
paper.authors_short: A. Calimera, A. Macii, E. Macii, M. Poncino
paper.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I · 2012
paper.text: In high-performance systems-on-chip, leakage power now rivals dynamic power, and memories suffer the most. This survey reviews the academic and industrial techniques that minimize subthreshold leakage in SRAMs, from the cell level to architectures for system-level design.

home_summary: The EDA group works on Design Automation for standard digital CMOS circuits, Beyond-CMOS technologies and Electrical Energy Systems. We develop CAD algorithms and prototype tools for low-power, variation-tolerant integrated circuits, model Graphene-based devices for flexible, ultra-low-power circuits, and build simulation and run-time charge and thermal management for hybrid-source energy systems.

name: Bioinformatics
intro: Our research automates the management, analysis and interpretation of complex biological and medical data through software and hardware-software solutions. Activities include gene expression data mining to find molecular targets for personalized therapies, regulatory network reconstruction, sequencing analysis to spot genetic abnormalities, image processing and pattern recognition, GPU and FPGA acceleration, and neuromorphic computing. We work closely with biologists, doctors and statisticians, and with hospitals.
funded_blurb: Our funded work reaches from the Human Brain Project and devices for neurocontrol and neurorehabilitation (DeNeCor) to personalized diagnosis and novel therapeutic targets for acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

paper.title: Automated segmentation of tissue images for computerized IHC analysis
paper.authors_full: Santa Di Cataldo, Elisa Ficarra, Andrea Acquaviva, Enrico Macii
paper.authors_short: S. Di Cataldo, E. Ficarra, A. Acquaviva, E. Macii
paper.venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine · 2010
paper.text: Two automated methods segment immunohistochemical tissue images: one recognizes the cancerous areas by unsupervised color clustering, the other the nuclear membranes of the cancer cells. Both prove more effective than approaches based on supervised learning or active contours.

home_summary: With long-term experience in bioinformatics, the EDA group designs software and hardware-software solutions to manage, analyze and interpret complex biological and medical data. Our work spans gene expression and regulatory networks, sequencing data, medical image analysis, GPU and FPGA acceleration and neuromorphic computing, with hospitals and research centers.

name: Smart City
intro: Pervasive devices deliver real-time data on environmental conditions and energy consumption, and middleware can make heterogeneous hardware and software sources interoperable, with an abstract view of their functionalities. Building on this, we develop a distributed software infrastructure that unifies energy, environmental and user-feedback data, presents it through visual web interfaces so users see the energy impact of their behavior in real time, and links building information models with live data.
funded_blurb: Ongoing projects include EEB, on zero-energy buildings in smart urban districts, and ITS, an intelligent transportation system, while past ones covered smart metering, district energy modelling and middleware for public spaces.

paper.title: IoT software infrastructure for Energy Management and Simulation in Smart Cities
paper.authors_full: F. G. Brundu, E. Patti, A. Osello, M. Del Giudice, N. Rapetti, A. Krylovskiy, M. Jahn, V. Verda, E. Guelpa, L. Rietto, A. Acquaviva
paper.authors_short: F. G. Brundu, E. Patti, A. Osello, M. Del Giudice, N. Rapetti, A. Krylovskiy, M. Jahn, V. Verda, E. Guelpa, L. Rietto, A. Acquaviva
paper.text: An IoT platform correlates near-real-time building energy profiles with sensor data and with building and grid models, to simulate new energy policies at district level. Deployed in a real district, it was used to develop and test a new control policy for the heating network.

project.title: DIMMER:
project.subtitle: district-level energy modeling and management
project.text: Coordinated by Politecnico di Torino, DIMMER links building and district-level 3D models with real-time sensor data and user feedback, to give occupants live feedback on their energy use. It was validated in public and private buildings in Turin and Manchester.

home_summary: ICT is key to optimizing energy use in the Smart City, and that is where our software solutions come in. We research distributed software and middleware that make energy, environmental and user-feedback data interoperable, visual web interfaces giving real-time feedback on energy impact, and building information models linked to real-time data.

name: Industry 4.0 and Smart Manufacturing
intro: Smart optimization of every step of a manufacturing process, from concept generation to production and product transaction, matters more and more, in traditional processes and new ones such as 3D printing and additive manufacturing. Our expertise in IoT technologies, cyber-physical systems, wireless sensor networks and machine learning supports innovative solutions for more efficient manufacturing of new products, dynamic response to product demand and real-time optimization of production and supply-chain networks.
funded_blurb: Our funded projects cover additive manufacturing (STAMP, MANUELA), shopfloor operation management (DISLOMAN), predictive maintenance with remote diagnostics and factory monitoring (SERENA) and metrology (MADEin4).

paper.title: Optimizing Quality Inspection and Control in Powder Bed Metal Additive Manufacturing: Challenges and Research Directions
paper.authors_full: Santa Di Cataldo, Sara Vinco, Gianvito Urgese, Flaviana Calignano, Elisa Ficarra, Alberto Macii, Enrico Macii
paper.authors_short: S. Di Cataldo, S. Vinco, G. Urgese, F. Calignano, E. Ficarra, A. Macii, E. Macii
paper.text: Additive manufacturing struggles to repeat its quality in mass production. This review covers the in situ sensing and machine-learning approaches that monitor and control metal powder bed fusion in real time, and sets out the open challenges and research directions.

project.title: SERENA:
project.subtitle: plug-and-play predictive maintenance
project.text: SERENA combines a cloud-based plug-and-play data platform, IoT sensing, AI-based analytics and augmented reality support for remote predictive maintenance, with demonstrators in white goods, metrology and elevator production. Politecnico di Torino is one of the project partners.
